title: Fraction to Per Cent
description: Grow both terms of a fraction until the denominator is 100, simplify first when it does not go into 100, or multiply by 100 in brackets and write the % sign last.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Write a fraction as a per cent through an equivalent fraction over 100 when its denominator goes into 100, simplify first when it does not, and use the bracketed method with the % sign last. A mixed number goes past 100%.
writeup.look: A fraction card over a bar of the same whole, the row of Times buttons, the Makes 100 counter, and on the later phases the brackets of the other method and a second whole bar.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Fraction to Per Cent' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the denominator the fraction card has reached. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The fraction card stands at x 110, y 230, 200 by 150, its numerator deep blue over the denominator. The bar lies under it at x 110, y 420, 600 long and 70 tall, labelled Whole and 100%, cut into as many equal parts as the denominator says, with the shaded parts deep blue. The Makes 100 counter stands at x 360, y 250 and goes green when the denominator reaches one hundred. The row of Times buttons runs along y 640 from x 110, each labelled in words. When both terms grow, the words Both terms light vermilion over the card, and the bar is recut into more, smaller parts while its shaded length holds still. The Divide by HCF and Times 100 buttons stand at x 760, y 250 and x 760, y 330. The brackets of the other method are written at x 760, y 440, the times one hundred step vermilion and the % sign in ink after the closing bracket. On the fourth phase a second whole bar joins at x 110, y 520, and the Unmix button stands beside the card. The per cent reached is green. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a fraction bar key, a space key for a mixed number and a % key. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. The part the question gives, as shaded cells, a fraction, a decimal or an amount, is deep blue, labelled Given. The per cent, fraction or decimal the working reaches, and what is left after a part is used, is green, labelled Answer or Left. Both terms multiplied or divided by one number, and the times one hundred step before the % sign, are vermilion, labelled Both terms or Times 100. A unit fact that puts two amounts in one unit is violet, labelled Unit fact. The part used, taken away or not won is rose, labelled Used or Not won. The step, cell or number being worked on now is amber. A zero holding a place open inside a decimal is grey, labelled Place holder, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded cell of a whole stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the % sign is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last fraction beside its equivalent over 100 and its per cent, with the bracketed line of the other method under it.

phases.win: the card reads 26/100, the bar is recut into a hundred parts, and the per cent card reads 26%
phases.does: taps the Times button that makes the denominator 100, and types the per cent
phases.goal: multiply both terms by one number until the denominator is 100, and the numerator is the per cent
phases.says: What times the bottom number makes a hundred? Do the same to the top.
phases.check: Away from the screen: why must the top number be multiplied by the same number as the bottom one?
phases.feels: the bar filling with thin new cut lines while the shading stays exactly still
phases.hands: Draw the fraction's bar on squared paper, then draw it again cut into one hundred equal parts, and count the shaded hundredths.
phases.tries: First rung: ask what times the denominator makes one hundred. Second rung: tap that button and read the new denominator. Third rung: the same task with a denominator that gets there in one step, before the question's own returns.

wrong.screen: the denominator past one hundred is lit amber, and the Makes 100 counter asks its question again with the child's product kept beside it

wrong.why: on the grid pages the numerator was the per cent, when the bottom number was already one hundred

wrong.screen: the bar is shown recut into hundredths beside the starting bar, the shaded hundredths are counted along it, and the denominator is lit amber

phases.screen: the card showing 13/50 over its bar, and the Makes 100 counter asking what times fifty makes a hundred
phases.soWhat: multiply both terms by one number until the denominator is one hundred, and the numerator is the per cent

phases.win: the card reads 11/20, then 55/100 and 55%, while the one third card climbs past a hundred and never lands on it
phases.does: taps Divide by HCF, then the Times button that makes 100, and tries the one third card
phases.goal: simplify first by the HCF when the denominator does not go into 100, and see one third never get there
phases.says: Sixty does not go into a hundred. Simplify first, then try again.
phases.check: Away from the screen: can one third be written with one hundred as its denominator? Why?
phases.feels: a stubborn fraction giving way the moment it is simplified
phases.hands: Write a fraction whose denominator does not go into one hundred. Find the HCF of its terms, divide both by it, and check the new denominator.

wrong.why: dividing one number felt like simplifying
wrong.move: divides only the numerator by the HCF

phases.screen: the card showing 33/60 with the Makes 100 counter unable to reach a hundred, and a one third card beside it
phases.soWhat: simplify first by the HCF when the denominator does not go into one hundred, and one third never gets there

phases.win: the line reads (21/35 x 100)% = 60%, with the % sign written after the closing bracket
phases.does: taps Times 100, watches the product worked out inside the brackets, and places the % sign
phases.goal: multiply the fraction by 100 inside brackets and write the % sign after them, the other method
phases.says: Times a hundred goes inside the brackets. The per cent sign goes last.
phases.check: Away from the screen: two methods can turn a fraction into a per cent. Should both be used at once?
phases.feels: the brackets closing and the % sign clicking into place after them
phases.hands: Write the fraction inside brackets on a card, then times one hundred, work out the product, and write the % sign last, outside the brackets.
phases.tries: First rung: write the fraction inside brackets. Second rung: add times one hundred and work out the product. Third rung: the same task with a denominator that goes into one hundred, before the question's own returns.

wrong.why: the sign belongs to the answer, and the answer seems to be on its way

wrong.screen: the sign tile goes back to its tray, and the product inside the brackets is lit amber until it is worked out

phases.screen: the card showing 21/35 and the Times 100 button lit

phases.win: the card reads 145/100 and the per cent card 145%, past the 100% mark on the bars
phases.does: taps Unmix, then the Times button that makes 100, and types the per cent
phases.goal: a mixed number becomes an improper fraction first. More than one whole is more than 100%

writeup.delight: On the second phase the one third card keeps growing its terms, and the moment its denominator jumps past one hundred, the Makes 100 counter gives a small sideways wobble and the card settles back to one third.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet tapped. On the first phase the fraction card sits over its bar with the Makes 100 counter asking its question. On the second the card shows a fraction whose denominator does not go into one hundred, with the one third card beside it. On the third the card sits with the Times 100 button lit and empty brackets under it. On the fourth the card shows a mixed number over one whole bar and part of a second. One thing moves, once: the Makes 100 counter, or the Unmix button on the fourth phase, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any fraction or mixed number, grown by the Times buttons, simplified, or put through the brackets. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on equivalent fractions over 100, simplifying first, the bracketed method and mixed numbers.
voiceLines: A fraction, and a bar of the same whole.
What times the bottom number makes a hundred? Do the same to the top.
Sixty does not go into a hundred. Simplify first, then try again.
Times a hundred goes inside the brackets. The per cent sign goes last.
One whole is a hundred per cent. Is this more or less than one whole?
A new fraction. Ask about the bottom number first.
Free play. Grow, simplify and bracket any fraction you like.
Look at the bottom number. What times it makes a hundred?
You made hundredths, and wrote the per cent sign last.

observations.why: multiplying both terms by one number names the same amount in smaller parts.
observations.soWhat: an equivalent fraction over one hundred names the same amount in hundredths.
observations.observe: The bar was recut into smaller parts, but its shaded length never changed.

observations.why: a denominator gets there only when, in lowest terms, it goes into 100.
observations.soWhat: simplify first, then check the denominator again.
observations.observe: Some denominators reached one hundred with one tap, and some needed Divide by HCF first.

observations.why: three does not go into one hundred.
observations.soWhat: some fractions have no equivalent fraction over one hundred, and saying so is a right answer.
observations.observe: The one third card climbed past one hundred and never landed on it.

observations.why: the sign belongs to the whole product.
observations.soWhat: the other method keeps its brackets, and the per cent sign comes last.
observations.observe: The % sign appeared only after the closing bracket.

phases.screen: the card showing 13/50 over its bar, and the Makes 100 counter asking what times fifty makes a hundred
phases.win: the card reads 26/100, the bar is recut into a hundred parts, and the per cent card reads 26%

ladder: Start with the bottom number, 50, and reach 100.
What times 50 makes 100?
Grow both terms until the bottom is 100.
Whatever the bottom is multiplied by, multiply the top by the same.
Once the bottom is 100, the top number is the per cent.

phases.win: the card reads 11/20, then 55/100 and 55%, while the one third card climbs past a hundred and never lands on it

ladder: Find the HCF of 33 and 60, and divide both terms by it.
Which number divides both 12 and 30?
Try the Times keys on 1/3 and watch the bottom.
Once both terms are divided, ask what times the new bottom makes 100.
When the bottom is 100, the top number is the per cent.

phases.screen: the card showing 21/35 and the Times 100 button lit
phases.win: the line reads (21/35 x 100)% = 60%, with the % sign written after the closing bracket

ladder: Find the times sign inside the brackets.
Which number is multiplied by 100 here?
Read the brackets: what is multiplied first?
Multiply the top by 100 and keep the bottom as it is.
Divide that product by the bottom to finish the brackets.

phases.screen: the card showing 1 9/20 over one whole bar and part of a second
phases.win: the card reads 145/100 and the per cent card 145%, past the 100% mark on the bars

ladder: Turn the whole 1 into twentieths and add them to the 9.
How many halves make 2 whole strips and a half?
Count every tenth in 1 1/10, the whole strip too.
One whole strip is 100%, so count the whole strips first.
Add 100% for each whole strip to the per cent of the last strip.

strip.label: 100% at the end of each whole

ladder: Count on in threes near 100 and see where you land.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: the denominator is lit amber, both terms are multiplied until it is 100 (the strip recut into hundredths, its shading still), and the per cent card shows the answer in green

Phase 2: the denominator is lit amber, both terms are divided by the HCF and then multiplied until it is 100, and the per cent card shows the answer in green; for 1/3 the products 96, 99 and 102 climb past 100 and never land on it
Phase 3: the brackets and the % sign are written, then the product inside the brackets is worked out on a second line, ending on the per cent in green

Phase 4: the denominator is lit amber, the whole strips are cut into the same parts (Unmix), both terms are multiplied until the bottom is 100, and the per cent card shows the answer, past the 100% mark, in green

voice.opening: A fraction, and a bar of the same whole.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Tap the card for a new fraction, then grow, simplify or bracket it.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You made hundredths, and wrote the per cent sign last.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

question.en: Now turn 43/50 into a per cent.
Simplify 12/30 first, then write it as a per cent.

items.planQuestion: Why can 1/3 never be written with a denominator of 100 by multiplying both terms by one whole number?

question.en: Can 1/3 get a denominator of 100 by multiplying both terms by one whole number?

items.planAnswer: Because 3 does not go into 100: 3 x 33 = 99 and 3 x 34 = 102, and no whole number times 3 makes 100

items.planQuestion: Write 21/35 as a per cent by multiplying it by 100 and writing the % sign.

question.en: Work out the brackets to write 21/35 as a per cent.

items.planQuestion: Write 3/6 as a per cent by multiplying it by 100 and writing the % sign.

question.en: Use the brackets to write 3/6 as a per cent.

items.planQuestion: Write 16/40 as a per cent by multiplying it by 100 and writing the % sign.

question.en: Write 18/40 as a per cent with times 100 in brackets.

items.planQuestion: Is 1 1/10 more or less than 100%? Write it as a per cent.

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

getState: toolId, mediaId, mode, mountPhase, phase, phases, conceptId, objectiveIds, step, steps, item, items, stage (teach, demo, ask, win, idle, summary, free), question, questionText, choices, typed, keypadOpen, tries, answered, firstTry, score, maxScore, answerShown (only after the answer), complete, questionCount, muted (the sound effects), speaking (always false: the lesson is silent), voice ("silent"), mascot, summaryRow, played, classroom, held (a classroom's parked piece of a long line), instruction (the pinned line), hint (the hint under it, or null), guideStep / guideSteps / guideOn (a guide-steps phase only), numerator, denominator, whole, w, factor, hcf, bracket, unmixed, complete

terminalEvent.name: finished
terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first

sounds: Web Audio, no files, on in every mode (the sound button switches them): correct, wrong (soft), win at a phase end, cheer at the last, a tick when a piece snaps, and cut, settle and trade where the picture moves
